taskDescription: Phase 3 MVP pilot: mechanism-level comparison of the attention gate (P002, research candidate) over the frozen Phase 2 CPU architecture, on the REAL licensed Oxford-IIIT Pet trimap slice. The candidate is a REAL published P6 product (candidate-P002) bound to a pinned implementation that passed the Phase 2 seven-step chain with CheckReport 22/22 and executable readiness=ready. The data is a real, CC BY-SA 4.0 dataset with pixel-level ground truth, prepared once and pinned by hash; what stays blocked is the independent test split, which only the formal final evaluation needs.
subsetSamplingNote: a seed-pinned random sample (seed 20261004) of 32 annotated images from the 7349 the dataset ships: 16 train / 16 validation, image-name disjoint. The dataset's own README encourages random splits, so the paper split is not used. This is a real dataset but a SMALL sample of it: it supports a mechanism-level comparison on real pixels and is NOT a benchmark. Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), from https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/data/pets/; attribution and share-alike both apply and copyright remains with the original owners of the images. The full source, archive hashes and preprocessing rule are in fixtures/real-data/oxford-pet-trimap-v1/manifest.json.
baselineValidityCriterion: PRE-DECLARED, and measured before it was declared: the baseline's validation_accuracy must exceed 0.5 (the 2-class random rate) AND exceed the 0.6875 majority-class rate of this slice's training split. scripts/probe-phase3-baseline-budget.ts measured the pinned baseline alone on this slice 鈥?5 steps 0.2500, 20 steps 0.4375, 50 steps 0.7500, 200 steps 0.7500 鈥?and the 50-step per-trial limit is the smallest budget at which both bars are cleared. A baseline below either bar would mean the matrix is measuring noise, and such a run is a protocol failure, not a negative result.
upstreamQualityNote: Phase 1 formalStatus=blocked, independentBenchmarkEstablished=false; sources are provisional. These disclosures ride every MVP report.

blockedFields.reason: the slice has a train/validation split and no independent test split; the SPEC makes the test handle an evaluation-side opaque id and blocks the FORMAL final evaluation when it is absent. This does not block the pilot, and the formal final evaluation refuses itself (CONFIG_INCOMPLETE) rather than scoring on validation data it already selected on.
